![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149397/assets/df0ffdd8bfb94ece82926411bfddb3affc85e802807a36cb2e8ee9b9b727633c.png)

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $x$-axis and the lines $y=x$ and $y=2-x$, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is $\lambda (x,y)=3x+2.$ Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type II region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,y\le x\le 2-y\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149397/assets/d1241b56d482f24cc06d51a9aaecbc623805df0a76739201e5cbe6974e2e9c6f.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $y=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-1|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y}^{2-y}(3x+2)|y-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y}^{2-y}(3x+2)(y-1)^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}-2y+1)[{\int }_{y}^{2-y}3x+2\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}-2y+1){[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+2x]}_{x=y}^{x=2-y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}-2y+1)[\frac{3}{2}(2-y)^{2}+2(2-y)-(\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}+2y)]\text{d}y \\  & =10{\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}-2y+1)(1-y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =10{\int }_{0}^{1}1-3y+3{y}^{2}-{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =10{[y-\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}+{y}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =10(1-\frac{3}{2}+1-\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,3\le x\le 5,\,\,0\le y\le 1\}.$
Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $y=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point on $D$ and the line $y=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-2|.
$$

Next, the area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=2\cdot 1=2.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{M}{2}|y-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{M}{2}(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{2}({\int }_{3}^{5}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{1}(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot [x]_{3}^{5}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}(y-2)^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{M}{2}(5-3)(\frac{1}{3}(1-2)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}(0-2)^{3}) \\  & =M(-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =\frac{7M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,\,-1\le y\le 1\}.$
Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $y=-2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point on $D$ and the line $y=-2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y+2|.
$$

Next, the area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=1\cdot 2=2.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{M}{2}|y+2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{M}{2}(y+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{2}({\int }_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{-1}^{1}(y+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot [x]_{1}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}(y+2)^{3}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{M}{2}(2-1)(\frac{1}{3}(1+2)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}(-1+2)^{3}) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}(9-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{13M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1\}.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to the square of its distance from the $y$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k{x}^{2},$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}k{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k({\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =k\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{2}\cdot [y]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{3}(8-0)(1-0) \\  & =\frac{8k}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=k{x}^{2}=\frac{3M}{8}{x}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3M}{8}{x}^{2}|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3M}{8}{x}^{2}(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{8}({\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{3M}{8}\cdot {[\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}-{x}^{4}+\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{2}\cdot {[y]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3M}{8}\cdot (\frac{32}{5}-16+\frac{32}{3})\cdot (1-0) \\  & =\frac{3M}{8}\cdot \frac{16}{15} \\  & =\frac{2M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-3\le x\le 0,\,\,1\le y\le 3\}.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to the square of its distance from the $x$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k{y}^{2},$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}{\int }_{1}^{3}k{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k({\int }_{-3}^{0}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{1}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =k\cdot [x]_{-3}^{0}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{k}{3}(0-(-3))(27-1) \\  & =26k.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=k{y}^{2}=\frac{M}{26}{y}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{M}{26}{y}^{2}|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{M}{26}{y}^{2}(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{26}({\int }_{-3}^{0}(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{1}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{26}\cdot {[\frac{(x-2)^{3}}{3}]}_{-3}^{0}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{M}{26}\cdot (-\frac{8}{3}+\frac{125}{3})\cdot (9-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{M}{26}\cdot 39\cdot \frac{26}{3} \\  & =13M.\end{aligned}
$$
